<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par136 />ing of the separate pronoun by {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=25}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽנׄכֹי}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}), and {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה הֵם|translate=these are}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=8}}; (''b'') ''of time'': {{GHGheb|text=עַתָּה זֶה|translate=now}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=24}}; ''just now'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=22}}; and rather frequently before words denoting number, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=36}} {{GHGheb|text=זֶה פַֽעֲמַ֫יִם|translate=twice, now}}; cf. 31:38, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; separated from the numeral in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=41}} {{GHGheb|text=זֶה־לִּי}} elliptically for ''this'', i.e. this present period, ''is to me'', i.e. makes altogether, ''twenty years'', &c. The other examples are similarly elliptical.<section end=par136 />

<section begin=par137 />{{GHGpar-heading|137|The Interrogative Pronouns}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|137|a}}
The interrogative pronoun {{GHGheb|text=מִי|translate=who}} may refer either to a masculine or feminine person ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=6}}), or even to a plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִי אַתֶּם|translate=who are ye?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִי־אֵ֫לֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=9}} (more minutely, {{GHGheb|text=מִי וָמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=8}}, i.e. ''who exactly, who in particular?''). It is used of the neuter only when the idea of a person is implied, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־שְׁכֶם|translate=who are the Shechemites?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=5}}; even more boldly, with the repetition of a {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} used personally, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=7|verse=18}}.—Another interrogative is {{GHGheb|text=אֵי־זֶה|translate=which, what?}}; of persons only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=5}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|137|b}}
Moreover, {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} may also be used in the sense of a genitive, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּת־מִי אַתְּ|translate=whose daughter art thou?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=55}}, 56, 58; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר מִי|translate=whose word?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=3}}; in the accusative, {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־מִי|translate=quemnam?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=8}}; with prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=14}} (in an abrupt question ''by whom?''); {{GHGheb|text=לְמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי מִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=15}}.—Similarly {{GHGheb|text=מָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַה־}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֶה|translate=what?}} is used for the nominative, or accusative, or genitive ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=9}}), or with prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עַל־מָה|translate=whereupon?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=6}}; ''why?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=32}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=עַד־מָה|translate=quousque?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=9}}.<ref>A quite different use of {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} was pointed out (privately) by P. Haupt in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=8}} ''will ye not tell him?'' i.e. ''I charge you that ye tell him'', and 7:1 = ''look now at the Shulamite'', corresponding to the late Arabic ''mâ tarâ'', ''just see! mâ taqûlu'', ''say now!'' It has long been recognized that {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} is used as a negative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=4}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|137|c}}
Rem. Both {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} are used also in indirect questions (on the merely relative distinction between direct and indirect questions in Hebrew, see the ''Interrogative Sentences''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=8}} (but read {{GHGheb|text=מְא֫וּמָה}} with Samar. and LXX), 43:22, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=1}}.—On the meaning of {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} as interrogatives is based also their use as ''indefinite pronouns'' (equivalent to ''quisquis, quodcunque'' or ''quicquam''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=10}} (read {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמַע}} in the apodosis), 54:15, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=4}}, 16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=36|verse=23}}; even {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמְרוּ־מִי|translate=have a care, whosoever ye be}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=12}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=לִי}} is to be read, with the LXX, for {{GHGheb|text=מִי}}); so also {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} (''whatever it be'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=22}}, 23; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וּדְבַר מַה־יַּרְאֵ֫נִי|translate=and whatsoever he showeth me}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מִי אֲשֶׁר|translate=whosoever}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=11}}, and {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר|translate=any man who}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=5}} ff.,<section end=par137 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
